_comment: PB-71 (docs/design/ARCHITECTURE.md Appendix B): the 27 README + 29 CHANGELOG documented-
README, §8.4 CHANGELOG). Every claim testable through the binary has a `documented` family
cell in testing/shadow-oracle/cells.json (status: "cell", the `cell` field names it); the two
rows ARCHITECTURE.md names CONTRADICTED get a cell that pins the CODE's actual behaviour
instead (status: "cell", `contradicted: true`). Claims that are pure prose — external
benchmarks, Docker/Kubernetes manifest literals busbar itself never observes, CI-pipeline-only
behaviour, Cargo/build metadata, or a bare pointer into another §'s own detailed cross-check —
are `status: "prose"` with a one-line `reason`, never silently dropped.
Not hand-maintained cell-existence: scripts/design-bindings.sh --check verifies the `cell` ids
referenced below still exist in testing/shadow-oracle/cells.json.

claims.quote: Six wire protocols, first class on both sides: OpenAI, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Gemini, Cohere and Bedrock Converse.
base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1", model = pool name
Anthropic SDK: pool name in the base URL (http://localhost:8080/fast)
client.responses.create(model="fast", …)
Gemini base_url="http://localhost:8080"
Cohere v2 client.chat(model="fast", …)
Bedrock Converse via SigV4 boto3
claims.reason: bedrock ingress is SigV4-signed; the plain http/exec/script drivers this family reuses carry no sigv4 signer, and the route itself is already exhaustively pinned by the llm.wire family's own sigv4-signed `llm|bedrock|*` cells — re-pinning it here would fake the signature or duplicate that family

claims.quote: BUSBAR_CONFIG=./config.yaml ./busbar &
Container one-liner: docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e ANTHROPIC_KEY -e BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN getbusbar/busbar
busbar --validate parses your config … and exits non-zero on anything wrong, with no server, no network and no state, so it belongs in CI.
config: { locked: true } for GitOps/read-only root
readinessProbe and livenessProbe both httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: http }
containerPort: 8080
claims.reason: a Kubernetes manifest literal enforced by the container runtime/scheduler, not by busbar itself; the underlying `listen:` mechanism it maps onto is already exercised generically by every other http-driver cell in the suite

claims.quote: runAsUser: 65532, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
claims.reason: a container/Kubernetes securityContext setting enforced by the runtime, not observable through any busbar HTTP/CLI surface

claims.quote: config: { locked: true } is what lets the root filesystem be read-only … Busbar refuses to boot without one.
claims.code_wins: boots, serves, WARNs 'config is READ-ONLY (the overlay backend is not writable)', refuses only admin-API mutations — never the boot itself (main.rs:856-865; config/overlay.rs:44-53)

claims.quote: observability over open standards: Prometheus, OTLP and a per-request audit webhook
native TLS and mTLS with no reverse proxy in front
claims.note: plain-TLS half proven live (self-signed cert, HTTPS /healthz, plain HTTP refused on the same port); full client-cert mTLS is the config plane's own parse-level fixture (config/tests/tests.rs test_tls_typo_and_removed_keys_rejected_at_parse)

claims.quote: The SemVer-protected contract is the runtime: the data-plane HTTP surface and the six wire-protocol contracts do not break inside a major version.
claims.reason: a stated release-process POLICY (CHANGELOG.md:320-323), not an in-process runtime behaviour a single request/response cell can exercise

claims.quote: config.yaml is an operator artifact, outside that freeze, and changes always ship with busbar --migrate-config and a loud fail-closed boot
Single Rust binary, MSRV 1.97, Apache-2.0.
claims.reason: Cargo.toml / build-system metadata, not a runtime behaviour

claims.quote: All performance / RSS / image-size figures (73 µs, 65.1 µs, 67,837 rps, 7.3 MiB, 5.74 MiB, comparison table)
claims.reason: external benchmark (onthebench.ai); the inventory itself marks it DOC-ONLY — no in-repo artifact to record against

claims.quote: Same-protocol routes are byte-for-byte identical … Busbar forwards your original bytes rather than re-serializing them.
claims.reason: the inventory marks this DOC-ONLY at this level, owned by the proxy/protocol inventory's own detailed cross-check (dialects), not re-verified here

claims.quote: Self-hosted, always. No hosted service, no signup, nothing phones home.
claims.reason: a negative claim about the absence of any hosted service; nothing in the binary to point a cell at

claims.quote: curl -fsSL https://getbusbar.com/install.sh | sh
claims.reason: install.sh is not in this tree (inventory: DOC-ONLY); nothing to boot or invoke

claims.quote: Helm chart https://getbusbar.github.io/helm-charts
claims.reason: no chart in this repo (inventory: DOC-ONLY)

claims.quote: five built-in routing policies
claims.reason: inventory marks this DOC-ONLY/unconfirmed — the only enumeration grep finds is a four-variant fallback set on a different axis (config/mod.rs:1306,:1343); no five-item surface exists to point a cell at

claims.quote: image: getbusbar/busbar:1.5.3 and "run against Busbar 1.5.3 while writing this file"
claims.reason: a stale doc pin (inventory: DOC-ONLY); not a runtime behaviour

claims.quote: 1.5.5: There is no config change and no behaviour change; only the log severity of two durable-audit write-through cases changes.
claims.reason: an umbrella meta-claim about the release; the two specific behaviours it summarizes are CHANGELOG:1088 and CHANGELOG:1090, not independently testable on their own

claims.quote: 1.5.5: The periodic write-behind flusher re-offers the audit tail to the durable store every tick (~10/s), and two of its skip paths logged a WARN on every one of those ticks
claims.reason: inventory points this row to §6 (its own detailed durable-audit cross-check); re-pinning the flusher's internal skip-path log-level here would duplicate that section rather than add a new binary-observable fact

claims.quote: 1.5.5: A recovered durable floor sitting ABOVE a freshly-numbered RAM-ring seq … is expected and benign, so it is now logged at DEBUG.
claims.reason: see §6; a durable-store internal recovery path, not producible through a single http/exec/script cell without the store-plugin fixture §6 already owns

claims.quote: 1.5.5: A permanent hash-chain gap … now WARNs exactly ONCE for a given gap seq … and logs at DEBUG on every subsequent flush of the same hole.
claims.reason: see §6; same durable-audit internals as CHANGELOG:1088/1089

claims.quote: 1.5.4: The Docker image starts again. docker run getbusbar/busbar:1.5.3 exited 1 before binding a port, with "the overlay backend … is not writable".
1.5.4: Busbar boots, serves traffic, warns clearly at startup that it has no durable config overlay, and refuses admin-API config changes outright …
1.5.4: The release pipeline boots the container image and checks /healthz before any tag … is allowed to point at it.
claims.reason: a CI/release-pipeline behaviour (outside the binary itself); the image declares no HEALTHCHECK (Dockerfile has none) so nothing in the running binary to point a cell at

claims.quote: 1.5.3: busbar --validate now resolves env: and file: secret references, and exits 1 when one of them cannot be resolved. …
1.5.3: Export sinks are named, and observability: is gone. … Move observability.otlp_url to an export sink using the otlp module.
claims.reason: PB-74 already freezes and pins EXPORT_MODULES membership as its own oracle-adjacent binding; a `documented` cell re-asserting the same module list would duplicate that pin rather than add a new fact

claims.quote: 1.5.3: Response headers are off by default. … observability.emit_server_timing no longer exists.
1.5.3: admin_insecure is now admin_require_mtls, with the meaning reversed …
1.5.3: A plugin's own log lines now reach your log sink … named by plugin, and are filtered by RUST_LOG like everything else.
claims.reason: inventory points this row to §5.7 (its own plugin-log-bridge cross-check); a real plugin-loaded boot is a heavier fixture than this family's reuse budget and would duplicate §5.7 rather than add a new fact

claims.quote: 1.5.3: Operational settings that were environment variables are now config keys: BUSBAR_PROVIDERS, BUSBAR_CONFIG_OVERLAY, BUSBAR_WORKER_THREADS, BUSBAR_UPSTREAM_HTTP1_ONLY and BUSBAR_UPSTREAM_H2_PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE. … the config key wins if you set both.
claims.code_wins: for BUSBAR_PROVIDERS the ENV VAR wins over providers_file: (main.rs:1645-1647 in the 1.5.5 tag); BUSBAR_CONFIG_OVERLAY is the only one of the five that actually matches the doc text

claims.quote: 1.5.3: The SSRF guard on an OTLP export sink checked only the literal text … the endpoint is now resolved and every resulting address is checked.
claims.reason: inventory points this row to §5 (its own SSRF cross-check); proving DNS-resolution-time address checking needs a DNS-mocking harness beyond a single http/exec/script cell

claims.quote: 1.5.3: advanced.worker_threads: 0 was silently ignored instead of reported.
1.5.3: Busbar could refuse to start in a writable directory when the config file was named with no directory path.
1.5.3: The request-log file export could grow without bound if the destination stalled, and every webhook export shared one queue limit
claims.reason: proving a per-sink queue-limit fix needs a stalled/slow destination double the http/exec/script drivers in this family's reuse budget do not provide; the per-sink gates themselves are unit-tested (export/file.rs, export/webhook.rs)

claims.quote: 1.5.2: auth.chain: [keys] with no way to mint an admin token now refuses to start. It previously booted as a silent open relay
1.5.1: /stats and /metrics report why a lane cannot take a request … and how many requests are parked.
1.5.1: busbar_lane_at_capacity is replaced by busbar_lane_available. Update dashboards that use it.
1.5.1: Retry-After on an exhaustion 503 always said one second under saturation, rather than the real cooldown.
1.5.1: limits.max_inbound_concurrent queued excess requests behind the cap instead of shedding them, so clients got no backpressure.
claims.reason: proving inbound shedding needs simultaneous in-flight requests (the existing `concurrent` driver, not http/exec/script); already the subject of the `concurrency` cell family (concurrency_cells()) elsewhere in this same file, not duplicated here

claims.quote: 1.5.1: Busbar no longer generates a signing key at boot. … 1.5.0 wrote this file itself beside your config, which boot-looped on a read-only mount.
1.5.0: The config file changed shape and a 1.x config refuses to start. Run busbar --migrate-config <old.yaml> > config.yaml … then run busbar --validate.
1.5.0: The per-key busbar_key_budget_remaining_cents gauge is gone with them, so use the bucket gauges.
1.5.0: POST /api/v1/admin/restart applies the settings that need a restart (listeners, TLS, store backend) without shell access.
1.5.0: busbar --validate covers the whole new surface with paste-ready fixes, and busbar --list-plugins prints the plugin inventory without loading plugin code.
1.5.0: Spend, budget-remaining and token metrics are labelled by group and window, and key labels set at mint time echo onto per-key series
1.5.0: A durable store is dropped and recreated on first open. Usage history resets with it.
claims.reason: inventory marks this DOC-ONLY here — store-plugin behaviour, outside this subsystem
